title: A TLS-Referenced Methodology for Evaluating Low-Cost Indoor LiDAR Mapping in Single- and Multi-Level Buildings: code and data
description:
Evaluation pipeline, analysis scripts and run-wise results for the article A TLS-Referenced Methodology for Evaluating Low-Cost Indoor LiDAR Mapping in Single- and Multi-Level Buildings, submitted to the Journal of Building Engineering.

Six open LiDAR–inertial SLAM algorithms — FAST-LIO2, POINT-LIO, D-LIO, HDMapping-LIO, LIO-LIVOX and the LiDAR-only baseline KISS-ICP — were run on 25 repeated handheld captures of two indoor scenarios, and every reconstruction was compared against a terrestrial laser scanning reference. The deposit contains the per-run metric tables behind every table, figure and statistical test in the article and its supplementary material, the rigid transformation of each of the 150 map–reference pairs with its RMS and inlier fraction, the element-level measurements of surface roughness, wall plumb and slab separation, and the complete code that turns one into the other.

Version 1.1.0 registers every map after levelling it with its own horizontal planes, because three of the six implementations export maps in a frame tilted by up to about 40 degrees from gravity; it adds the spatial hold-out verification of the registration, the levelled vertical ranges, the reduced-subindex sensitivity of the multicriteria ranking and the scripts behind them. The unlevelled results of version 1.0 are kept in data/v1_unlevelled/.

Everything the article reports can be regenerated from what is deposited here, without access to the raw recordings.
